structured_output.world_model: W5 (contrarian), after E016. (1) The tip at 0.7607 is E016's halved weight decay, applied to code that now runs at 9.5 epochs with 238 steps. Muon applies no weight decay, so the change only reaches the BN biases, the whitening bias and the head. I read the +0.33 pp over E015 as mostly a reshuffle. Its true expected value is about 0.758, so I centre every child forecast about 0.2-0.3 pp below the tip. (2) A mechanism nobody has named is spatial geometry, not pixel count. The 2x2 whitening conv has no padding, so 32 px gives final maps of 31→15→7→3 and 28 px gives 27→13→6→3. The 28 px phase therefore produces the same 3x3 map that the max-pool head sees at test time. Both 24 px and 20 px give a 2x2 final map. This fits two results. E007 (24/28/32) was neutral. E011 shortened the 3x3-geometry phases from 60% to 40% of steps, put 30% of steps at 20 px, and lost 1.4 pp. So dropping the 28 px phase (I023) should cost more than its pixel share suggests. Cutting 24 px epochs (I024) should be the cheaper trim. (3) Time is GPU FLOPs plus about 0.3 s of fixed cost. A 24 px epoch costs about 0.5 s and the average epoch about 0.66 s. (4) Scalar optimizer knobs are flat to within about ±0.3 pp. Structural changes such as width and batch size move accuracy by 0.4-1 pp.

forecasts.reason: Saves about 8% of compute. But 28 px shares the 3x3 final-map geometry with 32 px and 24 px does not, so dropping it should cost about 0.5 pp, more than its pixel share suggests.
Early 24 px epochs are cheap in accuracy and the 3x3-geometry phases are kept intact. Expect about -0.3 pp for about -6% time, which is a better slope than a uniform trim.
Same binary is likely bit-identical, as in E012. A fresh max-autotune cache could reselect kernels, but that is unlikely. I expect held-out seeds to come in about 0.2-0.4 pp lower.
1.5x more Muon steps with the same per-step lr gives more movement and accuracy. But smaller batches use the GPU less efficiently and Newton-Schulz runs per step, so time rises about 10%.
Scalar knobs on Muon+Lookahead have been flat; I expect a reshuffle plus regression from the lucky tip.
About 12-15% fewer FLOPs. But E010's smaller cut already cost 0.43 pp, and the main width group matters more for 100 classes. Accuracy probably lands near or below the bar.

cruxes: Does the final-map geometry (3x3 at 28 and 32 px, 2x2 at 20 and 24 px) rather than pixel count decide how much the low-resolution phases cost? I023 against I024 tests this directly. An alternative is 26 px instead of 24 px, which also gives a 3x3 final map.
What is the held-out (seeds 3-12) mean of the tip? If it is below 0.756, the margin is illusory and no time cut is safe.
Is E016's weight-decay gain real (it only touches the BN biases, the whitening bias and the head) or a reshuffle? This sets how much of the 0.76 margin can be spent on epochs or width.
